title: CSRF Protection

searches.query: "CSRF" interview SameSite CORS origin double submit cookie
searches.result: success; exact-concept search executed, but independent frequency/rank/company evidence was insufficient; prompts are original production adaptations and technical decisions use checked primary sources

sources.title: System Design Primer: Security
sources.supportRationale: Core conceptual orientation checked during specification; its brief section explicitly needs updates and is not the sole protocol/crypto authority or evidence of interview frequency.

sources.title: OWASP: Cross-Site Request Forgery Prevention Cheat Sheet
sources.supportRationale: Framework token protection, signed/session-bound double submit, origin and SameSite defense boundaries; CORS is not universal CSRF protection.

sources.title: OWASP: Authorization Cheat Sheet
sources.supportRationale: Least privilege, default denial and resource/action authorization on every request, with trusted enforcement and failure handling.

sources.title: OWASP: Session Management Cheat Sheet
sources.supportRationale: Opaque session lifecycle, cookie scope, regeneration, expiry and server-side invalidation; flags do not replace authorization/CSRF controls.

sources.title: IETF RFC 8725: JSON Web Token Best Current Practices
sources.supportRationale: Algorithm verification, trusted keys, issuer/audience and distinct JWT usage profiles; not a universal authorization or revocation protocol.

sources.title: OWASP: Cross Site Scripting Prevention Cheat Sheet
sources.supportRationale: Context-specific encoding, safe sinks, maintained rich-HTML sanitization and CSP defense in depth.

sources.title: OWASP: Authentication Cheat Sheet
sources.supportRationale: Identity proof, reauthentication, safe responses and protection of authentication endpoints; deployment-specific choices remain explicit.

scenarios.theme: An attacker cannot read the response but changes a victim’s email. Why?
scenarios.assumptions: The cookie-authenticated endpoint accepts a forged state-changing request. What will you do and why?
scenarios.limitations: Constructed production interview prompt; exact frequency, ranking and company attribution are unverified.

concept-specificity.rationale: Applies CSRF Protection to no read.

distinctness.rationale: Separate constraint/decision: An attacker cannot read the response but changes a victim’s email. Why?

production-prompt.rationale: Prompt states a production failure or workload bound and asks for a justified response.

direct-answer.rationale: Reviewed action: Use the supported framework CSRF/session and appropriate origin checks before the mutation, then authorize the account/action and required assurance.

decision-costs.rationale: Reviewed cost/alternative: Token/origin integration adds work

follow-up.rationale: Reviewed trap: Blocking response access via CORS cannot undo an already accepted change.

evidence.rationale: Primary support mapped to csrf, authz; interview frequency is not claimed.

full-delivery.rationale: Three labeled parts are self-contained; native disclosure and host confidence integration use stable keys.

scenarios.theme: The team replaces the session ID with a JWT cookie and removes CSRF checks. Is that justified?
scenarios.assumptions: The browser still attaches the authentication cookie automatically. What will you do and why?
scenarios.limitations: Constructed production interview prompt; exact frequency, ranking and company attribution are unverified.

concept-specificity.rationale: Applies CSRF Protection to jwt cookie.

distinctness.rationale: Separate constraint/decision: The team replaces the session ID with a JWT cookie and removes CSRF checks. Is that justified?

production-prompt.rationale: Prompt states a production failure or workload bound and asks for a justified response.

direct-answer.rationale: Reviewed action: Retain protection appropriate to the ambient-cookie request model and separately validate the JWT profile/lifecycle

decision-costs.rationale: Reviewed cost/alternative: A deliberate explicitly attached bearer-header architecture has different classical CSRF assumptions but retains XSS/token risks

follow-up.rationale: Reviewed trap: A JWT label does not decide browser request intent.

evidence.rationale: Primary support mapped to csrf, session, jwt; interview frequency is not claimed.

full-delivery.rationale: Three labeled parts are self-contained; native disclosure and host confidence integration use stable keys.

scenarios.theme: Untrusted tenant content on a sibling host reaches the app despite SameSite. What changes?
scenarios.assumptions: Those hosts share a browser site but are not the same origin. What will you do and why?
scenarios.limitations: Constructed production interview prompt; exact frequency, ranking and company attribution are unverified.

concept-specificity.rationale: Applies CSRF Protection to sibling tenant.

distinctness.rationale: Separate constraint/decision: Untrusted tenant content on a sibling host reaches the app despite SameSite. What changes?

production-prompt.rationale: Prompt states a production failure or workload bound and asks for a justified response.

direct-answer.rationale: Reviewed action: Treat sibling trust explicitly, enforce strict expected-origin and supported token policy, and consider domain isolation when untrusted content should not

decision-costs.rationale: Reviewed cost/alternative: Separate domains and stricter checks add operational/client complexity

follow-up.rationale: Reviewed trap: SameSite alone cannot provide origin-level isolation under this site relationship.

evidence.rationale: Primary support mapped to csrf; interview frequency is not claimed.

full-delivery.rationale: Three labeled parts are self-contained; native disclosure and host confidence integration use stable keys.

scenarios.theme: Matching cookie and body tokens are accepted after cookie planting. What is missing?
scenarios.assumptions: The chosen pattern does not authenticate/bind the token to the intended session. What will you do and why?
scenarios.limitations: Constructed production interview prompt; exact frequency, ranking and company attribution are unverified.

concept-specificity.rationale: Applies CSRF Protection to naive double.

distinctness.rationale: Separate constraint/decision: Matching cookie and body tokens are accepted after cookie planting. What is missing?

production-prompt.rationale: Prompt states a production failure or workload bound and asks for a justified response.

direct-answer.rationale: Reviewed action: Replace it with the framework’s supported signed/session-bound double-submit or synchronizer mechanism and test the actual cookie scope/injection threat.

decision-costs.rationale: Reviewed cost/alternative: Binding and key/session lifecycle add work

follow-up.rationale: Reviewed trap: Random-looking equality alone does not prove the attacker could not choose both values.

evidence.rationale: Primary support mapped to csrf; interview frequency is not claimed.

full-delivery.rationale: Three labeled parts are self-contained; native disclosure and host confidence integration use stable keys.

scenarios.theme: A cross-site link performs a state-changing GET. Will SameSite=Lax save it?
scenarios.assumptions: The endpoint mutates account state through a navigation-compatible request. What will you do and why?
scenarios.limitations: Constructed production interview prompt; exact frequency, ranking and company attribution are unverified.

concept-specificity.rationale: Applies CSRF Protection to get mutation.

distinctness.rationale: Separate constraint/decision: A cross-site link performs a state-changing GET. Will SameSite=Lax save it?

production-prompt.rationale: Prompt states a production failure or workload bound and asks for a justified response.

direct-answer.rationale: Reviewed action: Remove mutation from safe-method handling, require the proper state-changing operation and its supported CSRF/origin/authorization controls.

decision-costs.rationale: Reviewed cost/alternative: Clients may need migration

follow-up.rationale: Reviewed trap: Merely changing GET to POST without the remaining request checks does not finish the defense.

evidence.rationale: Primary support mapped to csrf; interview frequency is not claimed.

full-delivery.rationale: Three labeled parts are self-contained; native disclosure and host confidence integration use stable keys.

scenarios.theme: A script injected into the real app sends valid CSRF tokens. Is the token system broken?
scenarios.assumptions: The attacker’s code runs with trusted-origin browser capabilities. What will you do and why?
scenarios.limitations: Constructed production interview prompt; exact frequency, ranking and company attribution are unverified.

concept-specificity.rationale: Applies CSRF Protection to xss bypass.

distinctness.rationale: Separate constraint/decision: A script injected into the real app sends valid CSRF tokens. Is the token system broken?

production-prompt.rationale: Prompt states a production failure or workload bound and asks for a justified response.

direct-answer.rationale: Reviewed action: Fix the XSS source/sink, investigate effects and credential exposure, and retain correctly scoped CSRF/session/action controls rather than expecting them t

decision-costs.rationale: Reviewed cost/alternative: Layered defenses cost effort

follow-up.rationale: Reviewed trap: Stronger action assurance can limit some consequences, but CSRF tokens alone are not an XSS isolation mechanism.

evidence.rationale: Primary support mapped to csrf, xss, authn; interview frequency is not claimed.

full-delivery.rationale: Three labeled parts are self-contained; native disclosure and host confidence integration use stable keys.

publicDisclosure: Researched 2026-11-17. These are adapted production scenarios informed by concept-specific interview searches and the named references below. The System Design Primer provides core orientation where applicable; technical guarantees use the mapped primary sources. Exact interview frequency, rankings and company attribution were not independently verified. Security protocol and runtime examples state their assumptions; the questions test reasoning rather than a universal product recommendation.
